task.title: Let only a comment's author edit it
task.description:
Anyone can rewrite anyone else's comment, from the board and from the command line, and the rewritten comment is still shown under its original author with only an "edited" mark. On a hosted board that puts one person's words under a teammate's name, and coding agents read comments as instructions. Found by "Review the board for use by several people at once" and reproduced twice on 2026-11-21: bob commented from the command line, the board rewrote the comment, and both the web API and `workbook show` still named bob over the new text.

## Decisions

Decided by Dylan on 2026-11-21.

1. Only the person who wrote a comment can change its text. An edit by anyone else is refused, on the command line and on the board.
2. Anyone can still remove a comment. The thread shows who removed it.
3. This follows the rule assignments already have, and it is asserted identity like everything else: Workbook checks the acting name, not who is really behind it.

## To settle when building

- The acting person is the name "Record an edit under a name other than the checkout's Git email" introduced, taken from the operation's context.
- What a clone does with an edit operation that arrives from elsewhere and was recorded by someone other than the author (an older build, or two clones racing). It must be deterministic for every clone and must not silently drop anyone's intent; follow the concurrency rules in AGENTS.md.
- Whether the rule needs a new format generation. If it does, the changelog has to say what that costs a team.

## Done when

- Editing another person's comment is refused with a clear validation error, from the command line and through the web API, and nothing is recorded.
- The author can still edit their own comment.
- Anyone can remove a comment, and the thread on the board and `workbook show` say who removed it.
- The board offers the edit control only on the reader's own comments.
- Operations already in history, and edits arriving from another clone, project the same way on every clone.
- `docs/reference.md` and `docs/architecture.md` describe the rule.
